question: Should OpenClaw treat persisted-session retirement and finite agent-task completion as separate lifecycle events, and which of those should be exposed to workspace internal hooks?
rationale: Current reset, cron, webhook, agent-run, and subagent paths have different terminal semantics, while plugin and internal hooks are separate public surfaces; code alone cannot determine the intended permanent contract.

options.title: Separate lifecycle events
options.body: Keep `session_end` for session retirement and expose a distinct generic run-completion event for cron, webhook, agent, and subagent terminal outcomes.

options.title: Plugin hooks only
options.body: Declare typed `agent_end`, `subagent_ended`, cron status, and `session_end` hooks the supported integration path and document that HOOK.md automation does not receive a universal completion event.

options.title: Universal internal session:end
options.body: Add one internal `session:end` event across reset and finite-run paths, accepting a broader payload and more complex ordering contract.

recommendation.title: Separate lifecycle events
recommendation.body: Keep `session_end` for session retirement and expose a distinct generic run-completion event for cron, webhook, agent, and subagent terminal outcomes.

likelyOwner.reason: The active implementation discussion routes hooks and plugin API review to this owner area.
